name: decision-review
description: At a logged decision's horizon, put the prediction the user made back in front of them and ask what actually happened — one card, no model call, no nagging.

decision_id.help: The knowledge item id of the decision being reviewed — `decision_resolve` takes this same id.

summary.help: The decision in one line, as the user recorded it. Quoted back so the card is recognizable without opening anything.

expectation.help: What the user predicted would happen. This is the half of the record that makes the review worth doing.

confidence.help: The confidence the user stated at the time, 0-1. Shown alongside the expectation because a wrong call at 90% teaches more than a wrong call at 50%.

review_horizon.help: The horizon this review was scheduled for, as YYYY-MM-DD. Carried so a card delivered late says which date it was meant for.

metadata.why_free: One notification composed from the trigger's own inputs. There is deliberately no model call: the card quotes the user's own words back, and a summarizer here would paraphrase away the exact expectation the review exists to compare against.

steering_examples.description: The 90-day horizon on 'take the contract instead of the salaried role' has arrived — put my stated expectation back in front of me and ask what happened.
The card is landing while I am mid-quarter and cannot judge the outcome yet — resolve it 'too_early' so the review re-arms once rather than nagging.

example_outputs: one inbox card quoting the decision, its expectation and its stated confidence, with the id to resolve it against
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for logging a decision or capturing its outcome — `log_decision` creates the entry and schedules this review, and `decision_resolve` is what writes the outcome and its lesson

children.label: Put the prediction back in front of the user
